query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the selective laser melting (SLM) process parameters can improve the dimensional precision and mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components while reducing fabrication-induced defects.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy (HEA) powders, such as AlCoCrFeNi, with a diameter range of 15~53 μm
generation.intervention: Optimization of SLM process parameters, including laser energy density, scanning speed, and powder layer thickness
generation.conditions: Additive manufacturing using SLM, with a substrate material such as H13 steel, and a controlled atmosphere
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructure, including grain size, porosity, and defect density
generation.mechanism: The optimized SLM process parameters can lead to a more uniform microstructure, reduced porosity, and decreased defect density, resulting in improved mechanical properties and dimensional precision
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and toughness, and enhanced dimensional precision, with a reduction in fabrication-induced defects
generation.baseline: As-built HEA components with non-optimized SLM process parameters
generation.boundary: The optimization of SLM process parameters is limited by the material properties, such as the melting point and thermal conductivity, and the equipment capabilities
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between SLM process parameters and the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties is not fully understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: A designed experiment with varying SLM process parameters, such as laser energy density and scanning speed, and measuring the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties
measurements: Microstructure analysis using SEM and EBSD
Mechanical testing, including tensile and compression tests
Dimensional precision measurement using optical microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized SLM process parameters do not result in improved mechanical properties and dimensional precision, and a reduction in fabrication-induced defects, then the hypothesis is falsified

Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.

AbstractThe equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy (HEA) possesses excellent properties including exceptional strength–ductility synergy, high corrosion resistance, and good thermal stability. Selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing facilitates the convenient fabrication of the CoCrFeNiMn HEA parts with complex geometries. Here, the SLM process optimization was conducted to achieve a high relative density of as-built CoCrFeNiMn HEA bulks. The mechanisms of process-induced defects and process control were elucidated. The microscale mechanical behaviors were analyzed through in situ scanning electron microscopy observation during the compression tests on micro-pillars of the as-built HEA. The stress–strain characteristics by repeated slip and mechanism of “dislocation avalanche” during the compression of micro-pillars were discussed. The high-cycle fatigue tests of the as-built HEA were performed. It was found that a large number of nano-twins were induced by the fatigue, causing a non-negligible cycle softening phenomenon.
